A.explanation: Uses $1.0$ as the frequency in $\text{Hz}$ without converting $1.0 \text{ ns}$ to seconds, then pairs it with an impossible wavelength.

B.explanation: Uses $10^6$ for the nano prefix instead of $10^{-9}$, giving a frequency $1000$ times too small and wavelength $1000$ times too large.

C.explanation: Frequency $f = 1/T = 1.0 \times 10^9 \text{ Hz}$ and wavelength $\lambda = c/f = 0.30 \text{ m}$ with $c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: Treats nano as $10^{-12}$ like pico, giving $f = 1.0 \times 10^{12} \text{ Hz}$ and $\lambda = 3.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}$.

hints: Start with the given period $T = 1.0 \text{ ns}$ and write it in seconds using $1 \text{ ns} = 1.0 \times 10^{-9} \text{ s}$.
Connect period to frequency with $f = 1/T$ and check that $1$ divided by $10^{-9} \text{ s}$ gives a frequency in $\text{Hz}$ near $10^9$.
Then use the vacuum wave speed $c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ in $c = f\lambda$ to find $\lambda = c/f$ in $\text{m}$.
walkthrough: Write the period in base SI units: $T = 1.0 \text{ ns} = 1.0 \times 10^{-9} \text{ s}$.
Use the period-frequency relation $f = 1/T$. Substituting gives $f = 1/(1.0 \times 10^{-9} \text{ s}) = 1.0 \times 10^9 \text{ Hz}$.
Recall all electromagnetic waves in vacuum travel at $c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and obey $c = f\lambda$.
Rearrange for wavelength: $\lambda = c/f$. Substituting gives $\lambda = (3.0 \times 10^8)/(1.0 \times 10^9) = 0.30 \text{ m}$.
The pair $1.0 \times 10^9 \text{ Hz}$ and $0.30 \text{ m}$ matches the table row. This is option C.
